comments.content: Removing `outline` on `.cm-focused` with `!important` eliminates the only visible keyboard-focus indicator and no alternative (e.g. `:focus-visible` ring, border, or background change) is provided in this file. Keyboard / screen-reader users cannot tell when the editor has focus. Keep mouse aesthetics but restore an accessible indicator.

Constraining `.cm-content` to `max-width: 48rem` with `margin: 0 auto` makes a prose layout but breaks code editing: long lines will wrap early / horizontal scrolling becomes misaligned, gutters/line numbers (if added) won't align, and CodeMirror's measurement logic expects `.cm-content` to size to content, not to be centered with auto margins. This also wastes space on wide screens for diffs/tables/minified files.

Selection styling has no fallback if `--accent-soft` is undefined in a theme (transparent/invisible selection) and `!important` plus broad `::selection` overrides user / forced-colors / high-contrast selection. Also no `color` is set, so selected text may have insufficient contrast on custom `--accent-soft` backgrounds.

Selected search match uses `var(--warning)` background with `var(--background)` text with no fallbacks. If either variable is missing or low-contrast in light/dark themes (e.g. yellow warning on white background, or same-luminance dark-theme pair), the current match becomes unreadable. Verify contrast in all themes and add fallback colors.

Forcing `.cm-activeLine` to `transparent` removes the current-line cue with no replacement, hurting orientation in long files. If intentional for a minimal prose look, make it opt-in; otherwise use a subtle theme-aware highlight.

All --crepe-* tokens map to HeroUI vars with no fallback (e.g. var(--background), var(--overlay-shadow)). If any token is undefined in a theme / scope, or if this file loads before classic.css, the property becomes invalid-at-computed-value-time and editor surfaces fall back to initial/inherit (often transparent/black) with no visible error. Add fallbacks for at least background/foreground/border/shadow.

--crepe-color-background: var(--background, #fff);
  --crepe-color-on-background: var(--foreground, #111);

comments.content: --diagram-* vars (bg/line/border/text/1..6) are referenced ~40x with !important but never defined in this file and have no fallbacks. Missing definition renders as invalid fill/stroke (SVG defaults to black) and is hard to debug due to !important. Define them here or add fallbacks e.g. var(--diagram-bg, #fff).

Mutual exclusivity depends on upstream selectors (.codemirror-host/.hidden) plus :has() and sibling combinator. If upstream renames classes, reorders DOM (preview not a following sibling), or browser lacks :has, this fails open (code+preview both visible, doubling height) or fails closed. Keep the rule but don't rely on it alone — also handle the no-:has fallback in JS (toggle hidden on preview-panel) instead of pure CSS.

g > .node:nth-of-type(6n+i) counts by element type (g), not by class. Mermaid emits other <g> siblings (edgePath, edgeLabel, cluster) and version changes can reorder them, so colors shift/misalign. Combined with [style*="fill"] substring matching (misses `fill :`, uppercase, or presentation attributes) and !important, explicit user fills can be miscolored. Consider styling via Mermaid themeVars / init config instead of nth-of-type overrides.

Forcing rx/ry:0 flattens all non-cluster rects (including stadium/pill and rounded decision shapes Mermaid intended) and as CSS geometry properties has spotty support vs. presentation attributes. The universal drop-shadow filter below it creates a filter context per node/path and is expensive on large diagrams (scroll jank). Scope squaring/filter to specific shape classes and prefer a single container shadow if needed.

Global overflow:visible on foreignObject/labels fixes descender clipping but lets long labels overflow node shapes and overlap edges/clusters, especially since preview has overflow-x:auto (scroll container + visible children = overlapping scroll content). Prefer increasing Mermaid padding / line-height fix (already added below) without forcing visible on all labels, or scope to KaTeX only.

Asymmetric ProseMirror padding reserves left gutter for the block handle (4rem/3rem/2.25rem) but with max-width:52rem + box-sizing it shrinks usable width and can cause horizontal overflow on narrow viewports if handle is absolutely positioned or content has wide tables/code. Verify 320px viewport; consider using margin/padding only when handle is visible or switching to `padding-inline` with container query.

display:none on .gh-alert-marker keeps the literal `[!NOTE]` in the document for round-tripping but makes it uneditable, unselectable, and invisible to sighted keyboard/AT users — they cannot delete or change the alert type in the editor, and copy/paste loses the marker. Use visually-hidden (clip) technique so it remains focusable/editable, or render badge as non-editable decoration with marker still accessible.

Unprefixed svelte-select tokens on :root leak globally. `--list-background`, `--item-hover-bg`, `--input-color`, etc. are generic names consumed by svelte-select but defined on `:root`, so while the extension is installed they override/conflict with any other component using the same variable names. Scope them to the editor instead, e.g. `.jse-main, .jse-modal { ... }`. Same applies to `--zy-ring`/`--zy-field-ring` defined on `:root`.

Search-match foreground equals background: `--jse-search-match-background-color: var(--warning-soft)` and `--jse-search-match-color: var(--warning-soft)` paint text in its own background color, making tree-search hits unreadable. Combined with `--jse-search-match-outline: none` there is no fallback edge. Foreground should be a text token (e.g. `var(--foreground)` or `var(--warning-foreground)`).

  --jse-search-match-color: var(--foreground);

comments.content: Brittle dependency on library internals: `[class*="modal-inner"]` relies on vanilla-jsoneditor's current markup/class substring, and the surrounding chrome rules rely on heavy `!important` plus late stylesheet injection order to win. A library upgrade that renames the inner wrapper or changes specificity/injection order will silently break modal clipping, header and button styling. Pin/document the tested library version and prefer stable public selectors where possible.

Dark-mode coverage is a single token flip. `:root[data-theme="dark"]` only flips `--jse-theme` while every other color assumes App.css tokens flip correctly. This (a) never matches if the app puts `data-theme` on `body`/a wrapper instead of `html` (`:root` is `html`), (b) leaves non-binary palettes stuck with `--jse-theme: light` so library-internal light/dark branches (code theme, picker) are wrong, and (c) leaves `color-mix()`/overlay contrast in dark palettes unverified.

Focus outline removal depends on custom ring tokens. Multiple rules use `outline: none !important` + `box-shadow: var(--zy-ring)/var(--zy-field-ring)` where the rings reference `var(--focus)`/`var(--background)`. If those tokens are missing/misspelled, or a focusable path is not covered (inputs, selects, table controls, CodeMirror), keyboard focus becomes invisible. Keep a fallback outline or use `:focus-visible { outline: ...; box-shadow: ... }` so failure of the variable does not remove all indication. Also `--zy-ring`'s inner `var(--background)` band mismatches on overlay surfaces (modal/menu) where the canvas is `var(--overlay)`.

No fallback for `color-mix()`. ~15 tokens/rules use `color-mix(in oklab, ...)` with no pre-declaration fallback. On browsers without `color-mix` the whole declaration is dropped and the editor silently falls back to vanilla-jsoneditor defaults (blue accent, yellow bars), breaking palette theming. Add plain fallbacks before the `color-mix` line or gate with `@supports`.
comments.suggestion_code:
--jse-theme-color-highlight: var(--accent);
  --jse-theme-color-highlight: color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 88%, var(--foreground));

comments.content: Global :root leakage + dead token: --zy-ring/--zy-field-ring are defined on :root from a per-bundle stylesheet, so they leak globally while the CSV bundle is loaded and collide with src/extensions/bundles/json.css which defines the same names on :root. --zy-ring is never used in this file (only --zy-field-ring is), so it is dead here. Scope the tokens to the Tabulator container instead.

color-mix without fallback: if color-mix(in oklab, ...) is unsupported the whole declaration is dropped and even rows become identical to odd rows (stripe lost). Provide a solid fallback first, then the color-mix override guarded by @supports.

Both the column-title editor (:focus) and the cell editing input remove outline/border and rely solely on box-shadow (inset 0 0 0 2px var(--focus) / var(--zy-field-ring)). If --focus/--zy-field-ring is unset, clipped, or in forced-colors/high-contrast mode where box-shadow is suppressed, focus becomes invisible. Keep a transparent outline for WHCM and add a forced-colors override.

Selection vs hover is order-dependent: .tabulator-row:hover (0,2,0 with :hover) has the same specificity as .tabulator-row-even / .tabulator-selected and there is no explicit selected+hover rule. Today selected wins only because it happens to come later; any reorder or Tabulator base-theme difference flips it so hover with var(--default) masks var(--accent-soft) selection and misleads row targeting. Add an explicit combined rule after both.

Firefox-only scrollbar theming: scrollbar-color on .tabulator-tableholder is ignored by Chromium/Safari, leaving scrollbars unthemed there. Add ::-webkit-scrollbar thumb/track rules (or scrollbar-width + webkit fallback) for consistency.

4px resize handle is a pointer/touch barrier with no keyboard equivalent surfaced here and no enlarged hit area. Users on touch or with motor impairments will struggle to grab it. Keep the visual 4px but expand the interactive area via background-clip / transparent border or a ::after hit slab.

No fallbacks for app/HeroUI tokens. Dozens of `--jse-*` map directly to `var(--background)`, `var(--accent)`, `var(--overlay)`, etc. with no fallback, so if this extension stylesheet loads without App.css tokens (standalone use, load-order race, renamed token) every declaration becomes invalid at computed-value time and the editor silently falls back to library defaults. Add fallbacks for at least the structural tokens, e.g. `var(--background, #fff)`.

Modal `overflow: hidden` clips escaping select lists. The comment below states the dialog must stay `overflow: visible` so svelte-select lists can escape, but this rule forces `overflow: hidden` on `.jse-modal` for corner clipping — dropdowns inside transform-wizard/query-language modals will be cut off. Clip corners on the inner panel instead and keep the outer visible.

`border: none !important` on popups removes the only boundary in forced-colors / high-contrast mode where `box-shadow` is suppressed. Keep a transparent border (e.g. `1px solid transparent`) so Windows High Contrast / `forced-color-adjust` still draws the menu, modal and search-box edges.

Unconventional `box-shadow` order for the color-picker token: `var(--border) 0 0 0 1px` puts the color before the lengths. Color-first is accepted by modern parsers but older ones and strict linters expect `<length>{2,4} <color>`; if `--border` ever holds a non-color (width token) the declaration breaks. Prefer `0 0 0 1px var(--border)`.

Missing fallback on `var(--field-radius)` for the select radius (and transparent active line). If `--field-radius` is undefined the svelte-select radius declaration is invalid; sibling field rules already use `var(--field-border-width, 0px)`-style fallbacks. Also `--jse-active-line-background-color: transparent` fully disables the current-line cue in tree/text mode — verify this loss of location feedback is intentional.

Cascade layers are unsupported on the old webviews this file claims to support (Safari <15.4 / macOS 10.15 WKWebView). On such engines `@layer` and `@import ... layer(...)` are dropped, so Tailwind v4 and all layered HeroUI sheets fail to load — the `@supports not (height:100dvh)` guard below only fixes shell height, not the missing stylesheet. Either raise the minimum WebView target or provide a non-layered fallback.

Unlayered imports (tw-animate-css, @heroui/styles/utilities and @heroui/styles/variants) beat all layered styles regardless of order, taking precedence over everything in theme/base/components/utilities layers including Tailwind utilities. If intentional for variants, assign explicitly e.g. layer(utilities); otherwise animations/utilities can silently override component fixes and dark: overrides. Verify compiled layer membership as wrapped files with internal @layer may create nested components.components sublayers.

`var(--white)` has no fallback. If the HeroUI theme sheet fails to load or renames the token, `--background` becomes guaranteed-invalid and `background: var(--background)` on html/body/#root falls back to transparent. Use `var(--white, #fff)`. Also only `--background` is whitened while `--surface`/separator tokens stay grey, so chrome vs document can still clash contrary to the comment.

Latte and tokyo-day omit --field-foreground and --accent-foreground that frappe/macchiato/mocha define while overriding --field-background/--accent, so input text and accent-button text contrast depends on an invisible base light value. Define both explicitly in each palette to keep palettes self-contained; otherwise brittle if the HeroUI default changes.

Light-mode diagram label colors fail contrast on white: `--diagram-3-text: #16a34a` (~3.3:1) and `--diagram-4-text: #d97706` (~3.1:1) are below WCAG AA 4.5:1 for small edge/node text, and they cannot be fixed by re-render since Mermaid bakes colors and only these tokens restyle. Darken both for light mode (e.g. #15803d / #b45309) and check `--diagram-edge-text: #334155` size usage.

Active-match text uses page background (`var(--background)`) instead of a warning foreground token: in light mode this is white text on `var(--warning, #f5a524)` (~1.9:1, unreadable); in dark palettes it happens to work. Use `var(--warning-foreground, #fff)` or an explicit high-contrast color. Note also `::highlight()` is Chromium/Safari-only — Firefox shows no match styling without a `mark`-based fallback.

Per comment `"" means follow the OS`, but `if (base && ...)` is falsy for `""` (and for `null` on first run), so `dataset.palette` is not set and a custom palette flashes even though `t` is persisted. Gate on `t` alone (validated) instead of `base`.

comments.content: No integrity verification before execution: the script downloads an EXE over HTTPS and immediately Unblock-File (removes MOTW/SmartScreen) + Start-Process /S with no hash or signature check. A compromised release, hijacked browser_download_url, or MITM (e.g. via env-controlled proxy) yields silent RCE as the current user. Publish SHA256 checksums (or sign the binary) and verify before executing.

Architecture detection relies only on $env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE, which lies under WOW64 (32-bit powershell on 64-bit Windows reports x86 and hides real arch in PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432). On ARM64 this can miss the native asset or mis-report in the 'No installer' error. Check PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432 first.

Anchor the regex, validate https + expected host, and strip directories with GetFileName.

Predictable TEMP path without guaranteed cleanup: Join-Path $env:TEMP $asset.name can collide with a pre-planted file and Remove-Item only runs on the success path — if Invoke-WebRequest/Unblock-File/Start-Process throws, the installer is left in TEMP. Use a unique temp dir/file + try/finally and add -UseBasicParsing for Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatibility.

### Top Issues

**1. Extension host runs unverified third-party code with path escape**
`src/extensions/loader.ts` joins raw `id` into FS paths (`../`, absolute paths escape root, recursive delete), then `Blob`-imports `index.js` and calls `activate()` with full page privileges — no sandbox, CSP, permissions, or signature check. `src/extensions/extensionManager.ts` compounds it: `ensureCurrent` skips on-disk hash re-verification and falls through to execution on fetch failure; failed reloads keep stale `activeRuntimes`; uninstall-then-load races resurrect CSS/`activate()` side-effects; `fetchBundle`/`downloadAndInstall` save JS-only bundles as current when CSS fetch fails. `src/extensions/types.ts` + `catalog.ts` allow `cssUrl` without `cssSha256`, unvalidated `checksums["*.js/css"]` lookups, and mutable `main` fallback that will fail `assertIntact`.

**2. Native PDF export is memory-unsafe and spoofable**
`src-tauri/src/lib.rs`: null-checked-only `WKWebView`/`NSWindow` pointers cast to `&T` with unbounded lifetime (use-after-free if window closes mid-job); frontend-supplied `path` flows into `remove_file` (error ignored) + `NSPrintJobSavingURL` then polled by `wait_for_pdf`; completion inferred from 3×100ms unchanged file size (stale 0-byte file reports `Ok`, real failures only surface as 120s timeout); concurrent `export_pdf` share global `PrintDoc.html/ready` (second job overwrites first, prints wrong doc/hangs); any fetch of `/ready` — including JS in user markdown being exported — signals printable, yielding blank/short PDFs.

**3. Unsanitized HTML/SVG injection in export and diagrams**
